questions.stem: The law of reflection states that:

options.text: The angle of reflection is always greater than the angle of incidence
The angle of incidence is always 90 degrees
Light always reflects in the same direction it came from
The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection

questions.explanation: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (i = r), measured from the normal.

options.text: A line parallel to the reflecting surface
An imaginary line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence

questions.explanation: The normal is an imaginary line drawn at right angles (90 degrees) to the reflecting surface at the point where the wave hits. All angles are measured from the normal.

options.text: Smooth, flat surfaces such as mirrors

questions.explanation: Specular (regular) reflection occurs at smooth, flat surfaces like mirrors and calm water, where all parallel rays reflect in the same direction, creating a clear image.

questions.stem: If light hits a mirror at an angle of incidence of 35 degrees, the angle of reflection will be:
questions.explanation: By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. If i = 35 degrees, then r = 35 degrees.

options.text: Parallel rays hit a rough surface and scatter in many directions
Light bends as it enters a new medium
Light is absorbed by the surface

questions.explanation: Diffuse reflection occurs when parallel rays hit a rough surface and are reflected in many different directions because the normal is different at each point on the uneven surface.

questions.stem: An image in a plane mirror is:

options.text: Virtual, upright, and the same size as the object

questions.explanation: A plane mirror produces a virtual image that is upright, the same size as the object, and appears to be the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.stem: An echo is an example of:
questions.explanation: An echo is produced when sound waves reflect off a hard surface (such as a cliff or building wall) and return to the listener.
